frase_gancho.texto: She is not a queen: he is a young man emerging from the jaws of a serpent.

puente_narrativo.texto: Not far from Uxmal, at Kabah, a temple was covered with stone faces. Look for an enormous mask with a long nose that curls upward.

guion_corto.texto: This limestone sculpture, about eighty centimeters tall, comes from Uxmal, in Yucatán. It is called the “Queen of Uxmal,” but today it is thought not to be a woman: it is a young noble, or initiate, emerging from the open jaws of a serpent. Look at the face: a furrowed brow, oval eyes and downturned lips, a stern expression. On the left cheek there is a mark in the shape of a serpent with a curved jaw, perhaps a ritual scarification. Across the forehead he wears a headband of beads. The jaws that surround him are a doorway: the passage from the world of the gods to the world of humans. It is an image of rebirth, and of a mistaken nickname that became famous.

guion_largo.texto:
How does a sculpture end up with the wrong name? This one has been called the “Queen of Uxmal” for a long time, and it is not a queen. Those who first saw it, so delicate, with its headband across the forehead, must have assumed it was a woman. The nickname stuck, and it is still here. Today it is thought to be a young man, a noble or an initiate, and what matters is not his sex but what he is doing: coming out of the jaws of a serpent.

You have seen that image before, in another form. In the Toltec Hall, the [coyote warrior](mna_s05_guerrero_coyote) has a human face emerging from the jaws of the animal. Here it is a serpent. For the Maya, the open jaws of the serpent or of the earth monster were a doorway: between the underworld and the surface, between the ancestors and the living. To come out of them was to be born anew, or to be recognized as someone with sacred power.

Now look at the expression. The brow is furrowed, the corners of the lips turn down, and the gaze is hard. There is no smile, as on the little smiling faces of the Gulf. There is seriousness, that of someone going through an important ceremony. And on the left cheek there is a small mark: the head of a fantastic serpent, in profile, with a jaw curved like a hook. It may be a scarification, a scar made on purpose, or a tattoo; something that, as with the [Adolescent of Tamuín](mna_s08_adolescente_huasteco), turns skin into a written page.

This face comes from a very special building. It was found in the Pyramid of the Magician (Pyramid of the Magician), at Uxmal, one of the most famous in Mexico. It is a curious pyramid: its corners are rounded, so it looks like an enormous drop of stone. And there is a legend about it: they say it was built in a single night by a dwarf, born from an egg, who had challenged the king of the city. It is only a legend, of course. The reality is different: the pyramid was not raised all at once, but in several stages, one on top of another, like a nesting doll. This sculpture was part of one of the inner facades, which were later hidden.

The style of Uxmal is called Puuc. It is recognized by its facades like stone mosaics, in which hundreds of precisely cut pieces form figures, faces and geometric patterns. It is a geometric, elegant and very orderly art. You will see another example right away, in the [mask of Kabah](mna_s09_mascaron_chaac).

One more anecdote about the name: it is not the only case. When visitors toured the Maya ruins, they christened the buildings with names that occurred to them: “House of the Magician,” “Governor’s Palace,” “Nunnery Quadrangle.” None of those names is Maya. They were given by friars, travelers and explorers of past centuries, and they stuck. The true names, almost all of them, were lost.

So the next time you see a plaque with a pretty name at a ruin, ask yourself how much of that name is ancient and how much we added ourselves.

texto: Look at the face: what expression does it have?
Find the serpent-shaped mark on the left cheek
Notice the headband of beads across the forehead

texto.Origin: Uxmal, Yucatán (substructure of the Pyramid of the Magician)
texto.Dimensions: 80 cm high x 24 cm wide x 99 cm thick

texto.pregunta: Myth: The “Queen of Uxmal” is the portrait of a Maya queen.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The name is an old nickname. Today it is thought to represent a young noble emerging from the jaws of a serpent.
